challenge.better_approach: Considered option (b), a one-off caller check recorded on each verdict, and Akien chose (a) on 2026-11-17 because a command makes the rule physics. Considered judging callers by AST imports alone: it misses path callers (subprocess, bin commands) and cannot tell a fixture from a use, so running the namers' proofs measures it instead.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That every real caller has a proof that runs it. A caller with no proof slips through; the command reports namers with no proof to run so that gap is loud, not hidden.
challenge.prior_art: Searched the congruency lab for retire: codemother's constraint retirement and clearance's retirement_of (intention superseded) are different things; no command deletes code. The in-house prior art is bin/proofs/test_retired_components_are_gone.py itself, which this replaces.
challenge.real_collision: Law 8 wants a proof before PROVED; the proof here is of the command (a tool), not of a deletion, so no standing stays-gone proof is created. A distinction, not a collision.

answers.falsifier: Done when, over a scratch repo, retire deletes a target whose namers' proofs stay green, and restores a target and names the caller when a namer's proof reds; and when the live first use leaves bin/proofs/test_retired_components_are_gone.py gone with every namer's proof green. Wrong intent if a mention-only file (a fixture) is read as a caller, or if a caller whose proof does not exist slips through unnoticed and the command claims safety it did not measure.
answers.from_idea: none, because the idea was born in chat and is already settled at outline 1.3.7.1.1 (cairn/devices/cairn/requirements/01-the-rungs.md), Akien 2026-11-17 choosing option (a)
answers.how: cairn codemother retire <path>... (cairn/devices/codemother/bin/retire -> machines/retire): list the repo files that name each target (records, validations and dot-files skipped); delete the targets; run, by the tester's door, the proofs among the namers plus the proofs of each component whose code names a target; if any runs red, restore every target from git and name the caller; else report what was deleted and which proofs stayed green. First use: retire bin/proofs/test_retired_components_are_gone.py and bin/validations/test_retired_components_are_gone.json after repointing the four files that cite it; red ticket be4c6edef91b then crosses RETIRED.
answers.traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics: outline 1.3.7.1.1 becomes the command) and Law 5 (the working surface carries what is going on now; a standing proof that a thing stays gone is history kept as code).
answers.what: A retirement checks its callers in the same act as the deletion, through one command, so no standing proof has to keep checking that a thing stays gone.

bullets.text: cairn codemother retire turns outline 1.3.7.1.1 into a command: delete, run the namers' proofs, restore on red.
A caller is told from a mention by running proofs, not by reading text: a fixture that only names the path stays green.
